Meet the Warren Buffett Rule That Makes This Consumer Stock a Buy With $1,000 Right Now

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that shortly after buying Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB -0.36%)(BRKA -0.47%), Warren Buffett picked up a Baltimore department store because it looked like a bargain.
  • I keep coming back to that rule, because one of my favorite unglamorous retailers finally has a fair price.
  • Tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) sells what rural life runs on: animal feed, pet food, fencing, and tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:27PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Tractor Supply ›.

It has been revealed that shortly after buying Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB -0.36%)(BRKA -0.47%), Warren Buffett picked up a Baltimore department store because it looked like a bargain. Three years later, he wrote that he "was lucky to sell the business for about what I had paid." His lesson became one of his most quoted lines: "It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.".

I keep coming back to that rule, because one of my favorite unglamorous retailers finally has a fair price.

Tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) sells what rural life runs on: animal feed, pet food, fencing, and tools. It's the largest rural lifestyle retailer in the U.S., with nearly 2,500 stores.

This year has been bumpy. A rough May dragged down the second quarter, and the company cut its outlook in July. Bigger purchases remain soft, and CEO Hal Lawton remarked, "Elevated interest rates and reduced housing mobility are weighing on property improvements and larger projects.".

According to recent reports, the everyday stuff held up, though. Consumables like animal feed and bedding beat the store average, and same-store sales went from negative in July to growing by September. Neighbor's Club loyalty members made up nearly 82% of sales, and CFO Kurt Barton put it plainly: "Tractor Supply remains a differentiated business with significant competitive advantages." A crowd that loyal is my kind of economic moat.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Management isn't waiting around. It used tariff refunds to cut prices on about 50 everyday essentials, raised its Freshpet cooler rollout to about 1,000 stores, and now has its Allivet pharmacy filling prescriptions for VIP Petcare, the mobile vet business it bought. On Nov. 12, it joined the platform of Uber Technologies, so shoppers can get dog food or garden supplies delivered. "The need for convenience doesn't stop at the city limits," mentioned Uber retail executive Nathan Bernheim, while Tractor Supply digital chief Matthew Rubin noted that "millions of Uber consumers have a upcoming way to discover Tractor Supply.".

Industry observers note that not every bet paid off. The company closed 74 money-losing Petsense pet stores last quarter, and higher fuel and freight costs squeezed margins.

The stock sits about 30% below its 52-week high at roughly 21 times earnings. That's no bargain-bin P/E ratio, and Buffett's rule claims it doesn't need to be. A $1,000 investment buys about 25 shares, and capital spending should drop below 4% of sales next year, freeing up cash for shareholders.

"Whether it is preparing for winter, caring for their animals, or maintaining their homes and properties, we have an key and critical role to play in their lives," Lawton said.

In that 1989 letter, Buffett also wrote that "time is the friend of the wonderful business." For a store people need every week, I'm happy to give it that time.

CAVA vs. On: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seena Hassouna – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:34PM EST.
  • Recent findings suggest that choosing between high-growth consumer favorites can be difficult for long-term investors.
  • CAVA is disrupting the fast-casual dining space with its Mediterranean-focused menu and expanding grocery line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seena Hassouna – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:34PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Cava Group ›.

Recent findings suggest that choosing between high-growth consumer favorites can be difficult for long-term investors. Both CAVA Group (CAVA -4.67%) and On (ONON -2.76%) are scaling rapidly, but which stock is the better addition to your portfolio?

CAVA is disrupting the fast-casual dining space with its Mediterranean-focused menu and expanding grocery line. Meanwhile, On is challenging established footwear giants by blending performance technology with high-fashion appeal. While both companies target premium consumers, their financial profiles and valuation multiples vary significantly as they approach the next several years of growth.

Industry observers note that CAVA operates a Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant brand that prioritizes fresh ingredients and customizable bowls. The manufacturer serves a diverse audience, with significant engagement from Millennial and Gen Z consumers across its 500 restaurant locations. Beyond physical dining rooms, the business expands its brand reach by selling dips and spreads through grocery distribution channels.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 4, 2026, revenue reached about $1.4 billion, which represents a 27% increase over the previous year. This rapid top-line growth helped the firm generate a net income of approximately $64.7 million. The upward trend in sales highlights the successful scaling of its restaurant network across 30 states and Washington, D.C.

The balance sheet shows a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.6x, which is entirely attributable to restaurant lease obligations, as CAVA has no borrowings. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 2.7x, indicating the company has $2.70 in current assets for every dollar of current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $26.1 million, representing the cash remaining after a company funds its operations and capital investments. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 8.2% of operating cash flow in the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025.

It has been revealed that on designs and sells premium performance footwear and apparel to a global customer base. The firm leverages a multi-channel strategy that includes its own e-commerce platform, 67 physical retail locations, and a vast network of wholesale partners. By focusing on engineering and distinctive design, the brand has established a strong foothold in the Americas, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.

Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $4.0 billion, an increase of about 17% compared to the prior period. Net income for those 12 months was approximately $526.8 million, resulting in a healthy net margin of roughly 13.1%. This double-digit net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining as profit, suggests strong pricing power in the sportswear market.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer maintains a conservative capital structure with a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x as of December 2025, driven by lease obligations rather than borrowings. Its current ratio of nearly 2.7x suggests a strong ability to cover short-term obligations with liquid assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, On generated about CHF 281 million in free cash flow, providing ample capital for further international expansion.

CAVA faces intense competition from established restaurant chains and other fast-casual brands. The company relies on a limited number of suppliers and single-source partners, which could lead to disruptions if those partners face operational issues. Scaling 500 existing restaurants to a national footprint target of around 1000 also requires significant capital and carries risks related to food safety incidents or cybersecurity compliance.

ON Holdings must contend with fierce rivalry from major global competitors such as Nike and Adidas. Because the brand relies on discretionary spending, any downturn in consumer confidence could negatively affect premium footwear sales. Expanding rapidly into markets like China and Hong Kong also introduces geopolitical and regulatory risks that could affect its global supply chain.

Sources indicate that on appears to be the more conservatively priced option because it carries a significantly lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio than CAVA Group. The P/S ratio measures the company's market value against its sales over the past twelve months.

*Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

On earns the edge because it charges less for the better business. It trades at a lower price-to-sales multiple than CAVA while maintaining several times the net margin, and that gap persists even after you strip out the one-time U.S. tariff refunds that padded its latest quarter. CAVA grew sales last quarter almost entirely by adding restaurants, while guest traffic at existing locations barely moved, and its stock price already assumes that expansion will continue to work. Management blamed part of the slowdown on a produce-safety scare that may fade, but the valuation leaves little cushion if it lingers.On carries its own risks. Wholesale partners in the Americas are ordering more cautiously in a heavily promotional market; fresh Section 301 tariffs are expected to raise costs for its products; and it sells a single discretionary category. Both stocks also trade partly on being trendy, which cuts both ways when consumer tastes turn. I would buy On for 2027, but I would not back up the truck. Build a starter position, add only if the fourth-quarter report highlights how much the refunds were hiding and wholesale holds up, and keep CAVA on a watch list until same-restaurant traffic recovers.

Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (335 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
  • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
  • Sources indicate that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Sources indicate that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the manufacturer has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vistra ›.

    According to recent reports, vistra (VST -7.17%) stock was swept up in the artificial intelligence (AI) sell-off in November, but its decline began well before this month's midterm elections. Power producers have faced regulatory scrutiny over rising consumer electricity prices and who foots the bill for data centers' growing energy demands.

    With the market weighing the AI data center build-out narrative, Vistra's beaten-down stock is worth buying the dip on before November ends. Here's why.

    After a strong performance in 2025, Vistra stock has fallen 20% this year. Regulators across major data center hubs have pushed back on electricity deals to ensure ratepayers don't end up paying for higher costs and grid expansions.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, midterm election results, notably in Texas, cast a shadow over the ongoing data center build-out. That mentioned, outgoing Governor Greg Abbott had already paused permits and ERCOT approvals while the grid operator audited grid impacts. Not only that, but evolving rules requiring data centers to bring their own energy favor Vistra, which is contracting directly with hyperscalers while adding capacity.

    Vistra has reached agreements with Meta Platforms and Amazon Web Services, and under these power purchase agreements, the hyperscalers are funding capacity uprates, addressing one of the biggest concerns while Vistra locks in long-term cash flow.

    Management forecasts adjusted EBITDA of $7.7 billion to $8.5 billion, and most of its 2027 capacity is already hedged, protecting near-term cash flows. The stock is down, and Vistra's management declared it would add another $1.5 billion to its share repurchase program, capitalizing on the beaten-down stock.

    For investors bullish on long-term power demand from data centers, Vistra stock is quite appealing at today's price, now trading at just 13 times its forecasted 2027 earnings.

    #62302. Tech Report: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit for Men by Age

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (581 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit for Men by Age

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.
    • Men's average Social Security benefits run higher than women's at every age.
    • Sources indicate that as of December 2025, the most recent data available, the average monthly benefit for men is $2,282.28, according to the Social Security Administration (SSA).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.

    Men's average Social Security benefits run higher than women's at every age. This article lays out the numbers to show how those benefits compare across the typical claiming window.

    Sources indicate that as of December 2025, the most recent data available, the average monthly benefit for men is $2,282.28, according to the Social Security Administration (SSA). The average for women is $1,872.43, creating a gender gap of $409.85 per month.

    Recent findings suggest that the gap is visible the moment workers become eligible for benefits. At age 62, men receive an average of $1,572.83 per month while women receive $1,285.50. This difference of nearly $300 a month persists and grows as retirees age.

    Recent findings suggest that the figures in the table below represent snapshots of everyone at a specific age today, regardless of when they first claimed. Your own benefit depends on your work history and when you choose to start your checks. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later.

    The data above is as of December 2025 and comes from the SSA's retired-worker records.

    Industry observers note that the higher male average reflects historical differences in lifetime earnings and years spent in the paid workforce. The SSA calculates your benefit based on your average wages across your 35 highest-earning years, adjusted for inflation and run through the primary insurance amount (PIA) formula.

    Industry observers note that longevity affects how long these checks last. A man who is 65 today is expected to live about 18 more years, while a woman of the same age is expected to live about 21 more years, according to the SSA.

    Sources indicate that social Security is designed to replace only about 40% of pre-retirement income. This share is well short of what most retirees need to cover their costs, so many rely on savings or other income sources.

    Annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) are designed to help these checks keep pace with inflation, though they often fall short. The 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment that will take effect in 2027 will add about $91 per month to the $2,529.62 average for 70-year-old men.

    Married men may be able to help their spouses get more from Social Security through spousal or survivor benefits. Once you claim your retirement benefit, your spouse becomes eligible to claim a spousal benefit, worth up to one-half of the amount you qualify for at your FRA, provided they're at least 62 at the time. They will only receive this amount if it's worth more than their own retirement benefit.

    It has been revealed that after you pass away, your spouse will become eligible for a survivor benefit, worth up to 100% of the amount you were receiving or eligible for at the time of your death. This can be a significant help to them, especially if you don't have a ton of personal savings.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    10 stocks we like better than Nu Holdings ›.

    These are interesting times, with Congressional upheaval in the United States amid an uncertain economic environment with rising interest rates, elevated inflation, and potentially slowing economic growth.

    It is typically not a great combination for most financial sector stocks, as the sector often serves as an economic bellwether and thrives when the economy is strong. The S&P 500 financials sector has returned just 2.7% year-to-date, which is among the worst performers among sectors.

    Many financial stocks have tumbled in recent weeks, caught up in the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 sell-off over the past month. Here are two financial stocks that are at or near 52-week lows that are good long-term buys, even amid the lackluster outlook for the sector in 2027.

    Nu Holdings (NU -4.65%) is the parent firm of Nubank, a Brazil-based bank and financial firm. Nu stock is down 28% year-to-date, but most of that has come in the past month, when the stock has plummeted 17% to its current $11.95 per share, which is hovering near a 52-week low.

    The reason for the swoon is almost entirely due to the results of the presidential election in October, where the liberal incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat the conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in a surprise victory.

    Most Brazilian stocks tanked after the Lula victory, as the challenger was seen as a better option to spur Brazil's economic growth. But Lula has been in office for three terms already, a time when Nu has been growing like a weed, so it seems like more of a knee-jerk reaction than anything to do with Nu's business model or prospects.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that for investors, it is a tremendous opportunity to buy the dip on this valuation reset. Nu stock is trading at just 11 times forward earnings and has a minuscule five-year P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 0.13, suggesting it is well undervalued relative to its long-term earnings.

    While Nu is the largest bank in Brazil, the low-overhead digital bank has expanded into Mexico and Colombia. And in September, it launched in the United States. Its growth has been impressive, as in the most recent quarter, revenue rose 37% year over year to a record $6.3 billion, gross profit jumped 35% to $2.6 billion, and net income climbed 31% to a record $1.1 billion.

    It has been revealed that nu added 3.7 million customers in Q3, bringing its total to 143 million globally. It has grown rapidly outside of Brazil, and the U.S. launch offers a longer-term growth opportunity as the U.S. build-out is expected to take 12 to 30 months.

    According to recent reports, fidelity National Financial (FNF +0.97%) is a leading provider of title insurance for the real estate market. So, it has struggled in recent years as home sales and refinancings have plummeted due to high interest rates and inflation. And the outlook doesn't look much better in 2027, with perhaps a gradual recovery potentially coming in 2028.

    Fidelity National stock is down about 22% year to date and is not far from its 52-week low, trading at around $42.60 per share. Its 52-week low came in late October at around $37 per share.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that but here are a few reasons why I like Fidelity National right now, despite the weak outlook for real estate. For one, the stock is trading at just 11 times earnings, which is the lowest it has been in four years. But the firm has been resilient during a difficult market.

    It has been revealed that revenue dropped about 10% last quarter to $3.6 billion, mostly due to the loss of revenue from the sale of its reinsurance business, which was undertaken to improve cash flow and strengthen the balance sheet. The capital from the reinsurance business will be used to invest in core areas. The title segment actually saw revenue increase year over year to $2.4 billion from $2.3 billion.

    Sources indicate that secondly, Fidelity National holds a majority stake in a secondary business, F&G Annuities & Life (FG -0.05%). This business had a strong quarter, excluding the sale of the reinsurance business, with assets before reinsurance rising 7% to $76 billion. Further, its total core sales in this segment rose about 5% to $2.3 billion in the quarter, driven by annuity sales.

    According to recent reports, this business should sustain Fidelity National during periods of high interest rates and sluggish real estate sales because higher interest rates translate to higher annuity rates and higher spreads. That, in turn, leads to more sales.

    The other piece that makes Fidelity National attractive is its excellent high-yield dividend. In Q3, it boosted its dividend 4% to $0.54 per share, marking the 15th consecutive year of dividend increases. Further, it offers a yield of 4.98% and a payout ratio of just 41%, suggesting the dividend is safe.

    Analysts rate FNF as an overwhelming buy, with a median price target of $55 per share, indicating 28% upside.

    • Could USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) be the right stock to put your money in right now?
    • Recent findings suggest that USA Rare Earth is a rare-earth mining company that wants to become a mine-to-magnet company.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than USA Rare Earth ›.

    It has been revealed that as of this writing on Nov. 19, the S&P 500 is tanking; indeed, the index is on track to notch its sixth consecutive day of losses. A few days ago, Nvidia's blockbuster earnings came and went without confetti -- or former CEO Jensen Huang. Widespread apprehension seems to pervade every nook and cranny of the stock market, as the uncertain future of artificial intelligence (AI) hangs over everything.

    So what about mining stocks? What about rare-earths? We still need critical minerals. Could USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) be the right stock to put your money in right now?

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that USA Rare Earth is a rare-earth mining company that wants to become a mine-to-magnet company. Its flagship mining project -- the Round Top deposit in Texas -- is presently under development, but its recent acquisition of the Brazilian mine Serra Verde means that USA Rare Earth is now an actual miner.

    It has been revealed that production at Serra Verde began in 2024, and in October 2026, the mine began shipping rare-earth materials to a U.S. government-backed buyer under a 15-year purchasing agreement.

    Those shipments have given USA Rare Earth something that many early-stage miners need badly: revenue. Still, it's nothing to write home about. Last quarter, USA Rare Earth generated about $3 million, notably missing Wall Street's expectations of $6.5 million. Worse, it reported an operating loss of about $141 million and an adjusted loss of $0.44 per share, more than double the $0.19 loss analysts expected.

    In today's market, with several macroeconomic headwinds blowing together, I want to encourage a cautious approach to USA Rare Earth.

    There's no question in my mind that rare-earth metals will be valuable in the future. We have plenty of uses for them, and their scarcity has many governments concerned. But that doesn't mean every rare-earth mining organization will be a winner on Wall Street, and for USA Rare Earth, two risks need to be considered.

    The first is that Round Top Deposit, its flagship project, is still in the exploration phase: Its commercial viability has not been determined. Even more concerning is the fact that miners have been trying to develop Round Top for decades without commercial success. Its history stretches back to the 1970s, when it was investigated for fluorite, and the asset has changed hands several times before coming under USA Rare Earth's control.

    The second risk to consider is rising interest rates. Even if Round Top proves economically valuable beyond the market's wildest dreams, USA Rare Earth will need substantial capital to bring the mine into production. Higher interest rates would make borrowing more expensive, likely forcing the organization to issue more shares and dilute existing investors.

    Between these risks and USA Rare Earth's mounting losses, I see more reasons to avoid this stock than to buy it right now.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that shares of Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) fell about 14% on Friday to close near $595.
    • Micron closed at a record high of $1,213.56 on June 25, so the stock has lost about half its value over five months.
    • According to recent reports, but management noted in late September that customers had already committed to over three-quarters of Micron's planned shipments for this fiscal year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:52PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

    It has been revealed that shares of Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) fell about 14% on Friday to close near $595. That's the lowest close for the memory chipmaker's stock since early May.

    Micron closed at a record high of $1,213.56 on June 25, so the stock has lost about half its value over five months. And memory stocks dropped across the board on Friday, with Sandisk down about 16%.

    According to recent reports, but management noted in late September that customers had already committed to over three-quarters of Micron's planned shipments for this fiscal year. At roughly $595, the stock costs about 3.5 times expected earnings for that year, fiscal 2027, which ends in early September 2027.

    I think the fall has more to do with worries over memory prices than with how much Micron can sell.

    Micron president and chief operating officer Manish Bhatia said on the tech giant's Sept. 30 earnings call that "we have more than 75% of our shipments committed for the year," referring to fiscal 2027. He added that this "allows us to shift our conversations on allocation with our customers out to 2028.".

    Put another way, buyers have mostly claimed their share of Micron's output through next September, and the talks have already moved on.

    In a recent development, the numbers back that up, helped by demand from artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. Micron's revenue in its fiscal fourth quarter, the 14 weeks ending Sept. 3, came to $54.2 billion. That was 31% higher than in the previous quarter and 379% above the year-ago quarter. Earnings per share climbed more than elevenfold year over year, to $32.87. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, management sees revenue of about $61.5 billion, roughly 13% above fiscal Q4, and it expects every quarter of the year to beat the one before.

    So growth is easing from a blistering pace. But it isn't reversing.

    It has been revealed that committed shipments, though, don't all come with committed prices. Micron's multiyear strategic customer agreements, which it estimates will make up over 35% of its revenue through 2030, are where it sets most prices ahead of time. Even in those deals, around a quarter of the expected revenue is priced periodically based on market prices.

    Industry observers note that that probably leaves most of Micron's sales linked to where memory prices head. And prices did a lot of the work last quarter.

    Industry observers note that in fiscal Q4, prices for Micron's DRAM (the short-term memory in servers, PCs, and phones) rose a high-teens percentage from the previous quarter. DRAM made up 73% of revenue. Prices for its NAND flash storage chips, 26% of revenue, climbed around 30%.

    According to recent reports, these price gains show in Micron's gross margin under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). It was 44.7% a year before, reached 84.6% by fiscal Q3, then hit 86.8% in fiscal Q4. Management's forecast for this quarter is around 86%. It expects margins to inch up over the rest of fiscal 2027, though with "a more moderate rate of price increases.".

    Industry observers note that there are early signs prices might ease. On Nov. 19, TrendForce predicted that NAND flash contract prices may drop 0% to 5% in the first quarter of 2027, with a broader downturn starting in the second quarter. Also, TrendForce remarked the average spot price for mainstream DDR4 memory chips dipped around 1% in the week ending Nov. 17, while branded DDR5 spot prices were mostly steady.

    Sure, a 1% dip in spot prices isn't a memory bust. But I'd track DRAM prices closely from here. After all, Micron's profits have ridden on rising prices.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that micron has plenty of room before lower prices erase its profits. The cost of the chips Micron sold was just around 13% of its revenue in fiscal Q4. Rough math indicates that if prices dropped 30% and these costs stayed flat, its gross margin would still be about 81%. That would be around where it was for all of fiscal 2026, and about double fiscal 2025's 39.8%.

    It has been revealed that of course, prices might drop more than that. And costs won't stand still while Micron keeps building. Its capital expenditures came to about $27.4 billion in fiscal 2026, almost double the year before.

    According to recent reports, but the stock price already allows for a steep fall in profits. Even on fiscal 2026's results, when Micron earned $74.33 per share, the stock costs just around 8 times earnings. On this year's expected earnings, it's under half that.

    In a recent development, I'd buy more here, albeit only if the position is still small even after my addition, and I'd keep Micron a small part of a diversified portfolio. Memory prices can turn fast, and the stock might drop further before they do.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    According to recent reports, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Sources indicate that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the organization like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo mentioned. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo remarked.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    By Matt DiLallo – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Verizon Communications ›.

    According to recent reports, verizon (VZ +1.62%) pays $0.7075 per share in dividends to its investors each quarter. At its recent share price, the telecom giant yields 6.2%, significantly higher than the S&P 500's 1.1%. Verizon's dividend costs about $2.9 billion per quarter, or around $11.7 billion annually.

    Here's a look at the free cash flow that supports its high-yielding dividend.

    Industry observers note that verizon generates substantial recurring revenue as customers pay their internet and broadband bills. It hauled in $34.3 billion of revenue during the third quarter, up 1.5% year over year. It has generated $103 billion of revenue during the first nine months of this year (up 1.2%).

    According to recent reports, the company converts a significant portion of its revenue into cash flow. Verizon generated $29.9 billion of cash flow from operations during the first nine months of this year, up nearly 7% compared to the year-ago period. The telecom giant spent $11.9 billion on capital expenditures to maintain and expand its networks, leaving it with $18 billion in free cash flow. That's up from $15.8 billion compared to the prior-year period. It was more than enough to cover the $8.8 billion Verizon paid in dividends. The company used its excess free cash flow to repurchase $4 billion of shares and strengthen its balance sheet.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that verizon currently expects to spend $16 billion to $16.5 billion on capital expenditures this year, down from $17 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, it now expects its free cash flow to increase by as much as 12% from last year's $20.1 billion, implying roughly $22.5 billion. That will cover its $11.7 billion in dividends nearly two times over.

    It has been revealed that that gives Verizon plenty of room to grow its dividend. The company delivered its 20th consecutive annual dividend increase earlier this year. It has been growing its payout at a modest low-single-digit rate, which should continue. That would still leave it with ample excess free cash flow to repurchase shares while continuing to strengthen its balance sheet. Verizon's debt has increased by $20 billion over the past year due to its acquisition of Frontier. However, it has a reasonable 2.3x leverage ratio (up from 2.2x in the year-ago period) and solid credit ratings (A-/BBB+/Baa1).

    According to recent reports, at over 6%, Verizon has one of the highest dividend yields in the S&P 500. However, it's not a high-risk dividend stock. The organization comfortably covers its payout with cash, providing it with excess to strengthen its already solid balance sheet and repurchase shares. While Verizon won't provide much growth, it can certainly provide investors with a lucrative, steadily rising stream of passive dividend income.

    If You’d Invested $10,000 in Rocket Lab 5 Years Ago, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today -- Even After a 60% Crash

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%) have fallen roughly 60% from their all-time highs in June 2026.
    • Industry observers note that benjamin Graham, the man who helped train Wall Street icon Warren Buffett, liked to say that Wall Street was a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Industry observers note that shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%) have fallen roughly 60% from their all-time highs in June 2026. That's a massive decline. And yet, even with that decline, a $10,000 investment in the stock five years ago would still be worth more than $33,000 as of this writing. There's an important backstory here, even as Space Exploration Corporation (SPCX -7.69%) makes the biggest headlines in the still-emerging space industry. Here's what you need to know.

    Industry observers note that benjamin Graham, the man who helped train Wall Street icon Warren Buffett, liked to say that Wall Street was a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term. The point here is that emotions are what move stock prices in the near term, while business success is recognized over the long term. Graham and Buffett both used this insight to highlight value investments, but it is equally important when considering growth stocks, assuming you have a long enough investment horizon.

    It has been revealed that that fact is on clear display in the space industry. There was massive enthusiasm for space-related stocks leading up to SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO). That enthusiasm petered out after the IPO. That's not particularly shocking, given the hype on Wall Street and Main Street around that IPO. Rocket Lab simply got caught up in the emotional swing since it is a SpaceX competitor. But that doesn't mean Rocket Lab isn't achieving success as a business.

    According to recent reports, recent news was flooded with results from SpaceX's Starship launch. On the negative side, the company failed to catch the spaceship's lower section (the booster rocket). On the positive side, it successfully caught the upper portion (the actual spacecraft). The end goal is to have a completely reusable rocket system, which would dramatically reduce the cost of getting to space. It is very exciting stuff.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that in the shadow of this industry leader, Rocket Lab achieved its own milestone on Nov. 14, 2026. That was the day the manufacturer marked the 100th launch of its Electron spacecraft. The company noted in a press release that it had set "a new record for reaching 100 releases faster than any other commercially developed rocket." SpaceX gets most of the headlines, but Rocket Lab is making progress as a business, too.

    To be fair, Rocket Lab is a money-losing start-up. So it isn't an appropriate investment for risk-averse investors. But it may be of interest to growth investors that have a long-term focus. The space industry is still in its early stages of development. SpaceX is the dominant player, but there will be room for more than one manufacturer.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that that's been highlighted recently by SpaceX's own satellite launch plans, which are limiting other companies' access to its rolls out. If the manufacturer increasingly focuses on its own business, it leaves companies with no other option but to turn to competitors like Rocket Lab. And given the success Rocket Lab has had with its own launches, investors are clearly recognizing the long-term opportunity even as emotional investors create material price volatility. That's why the stock is up so much over the long term but down so much over the short term.

    According to recent reports, rocket Lab isn't for the faint of heart, given that the stock is likely to remain volatile. And operating in the shadow of SpaceX won't help the situation any. However, Rocket Lab is making key progress as a business. Over the long term, assuming you can handle the volatility, it could be an attractive option in the still-emerging space industry.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the firm's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • In a recent development, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • Sources indicate that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the firm's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    In a recent development, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Sources indicate that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the organization to fulfill all of its previously confirmed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate newly introduced multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider remarked in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Industry observers note that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    Sources indicate that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Sources indicate that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The tech giant had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Industry observers note that neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    In a recent development, "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my firm every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    In a recent development, bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any significant changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real glitch is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    Iraola will be beaming: Liverpool handed massive double injury boost ahead of Man United clash

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.
    • Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.
    • The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.

    Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

    The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

    As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

    The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

    The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

    Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

    As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

    Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

    However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    Recent findings suggest that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    In a recent development, the major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Sources indicate that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    In a recent development, from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see fresh highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Empireofthekop ↗ Open Full Page

    Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
    • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.
    • The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

    The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

    The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

    However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

    The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

    ‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

    The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

    Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

    It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

    Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

    Welcome to our Live Comments section, where upcoming comments will appear automatically.

    It has been revealed that it was a clear and obvious mistake by the ref. I doubt anyone has seen a penalty awarded for an innocent clash of heads, so why was it that VAR ignored it? Incompetence by the referee and VAR or something else? Fed up with seeing such terrible officiating.

    #62231. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (633 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • In a recent development, however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    In a recent development, however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a significant haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the organization's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    In a recent development, this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    It has been revealed that this lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    #62224. Latest Update: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1112 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1112 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the tech giant as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks latest CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to swiftly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    Industry observers note that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    Recent findings suggest that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the organization's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway states it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

    According to recent reports, WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    It has been revealed that two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that claims it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Sources indicate that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Sources indicate that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, noted in a text ahead of the organization's after-market report on Tuesday.

    It has been revealed that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is presently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    In a recent development, one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (416 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.
    • The artificial intelligence company raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
    • Anthropic noted it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.

    The artificial intelligence company raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

    Anthropic noted it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe.".

    According to recent reports, shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in premarket trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

    According to recent reports, in addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic said Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

    Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry plans for a multitrillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

    CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the organization in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.

    The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone" in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but said there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

    In a recent development, "For us, it's like one stop on the journey," Daniela Amodei said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same organization.'".
